title: Peace after Waterloo
text: Napoleon was beaten at Waterloo on 18 June and has abdicated. The powers must pay for the wars and rebuild, and they will need bankers.

title: The Second Peace of Paris
text: The treaty signed on 20 November makes France pay an indemnity of 700 million francs and keep an allied army of occupation. French credit is strained.

title: London's mining shares collapse
text: The craze for Latin American mining shares is over. Shares that soared last winter have lost most of their value, Latin American bonds have halved, and the banks that lent against them are nervous.

title: Banks fail in London
text: In December Pole and Company and other London banks close their doors, and dozens of country banks follow. Bills drawn on London are refused at the Frankfurt bourse.

title: Panic reaches the continent
text: The London crisis spreads to the merchant houses of Europe. Frankfurt depositors want their money back, and they want it now.

title: Revolution in Paris
text: Three days of street fighting at the end of July drive Charles X from the throne. French bonds fall while investors wait to see what follows.

title: The Zollverein begins
text: A customs union led by Prussia takes effect across much of Germany. Frankfurt, a free city that lives by its own trade, stays outside for now.

title: Germany's first railway
text: On 7 December the locomotive Adler pulls the first train from Nuremberg to Fuerth. Railway companies will soon come looking for capital.

title: Frankfurt joins the Zollverein
text: The free city signs up to the customs union. Goods now cross from the Rhine to the Prussian east without tolls, and merchant credit is safer for it.

title: Commercial crisis in London
text: Speculation in corn and railways ends in October with a wave of failures among London trading houses. Credit tightens across Europe.

title: France is a republic again
text: After three days of fighting in late February, Louis-Philippe abdicates and a republic is proclaimed. French bonds tumble.

title: Revolution in Vienna and Berlin
text: In March crowds drive Metternich from power in Vienna, and Berlin fights its own soldiers in the streets. Every government in Germany looks shaky.

title: Fire in the Fahrgasse
text: A blaze destroys a merchant's warehouse and all his stock. He cannot repay the house.

title: A clerk caught skimming
text: A junior clerk has been taking small sums from the strongbox for months. He is caught, and waits in the back office to learn his fate.

options.label: Prosecute him in open court
options.text: The clerk is tried in open court. The bourse sees a house that guards its strongbox.

options.label: Dismiss him quietly
options.text: The clerk is dismissed without a word to anyone.

chance.text: Word gets out all the same, and the bourse wonders what else the house keeps quiet.
chance.miss_text: The matter never leaves the counting house.

options.label: Forgive him
options.text: The clerk is forgiven and kept on. The staff call it kindness; the partners call it weakness.

title: Rumours from Bankhaus Kessler
text: A rival house whispers on the bourse that your house is short of cash. Depositors are beginning to ask questions.

options.label: Ignore them
options.text: The rumours are left to run, and some depositors listen.

options.label: Open your books to the bourse
options.text: The house's books are opened to the leading merchants. The rumours die, though some wonder why it came to that.

options.label: Answer in kind
options.text: Your agents put it about that Kessler's own vaults are thin.

chance.text: One of them is caught at it, and it is your house that looks small.
chance.miss_text: Kessler's house takes its share of the whispers.

title: A good name
text: A respected merchant tells the bourse that your house has never once been late with a payment.

title: A good harvest
text: Full granaries across Hesse and the Palatinate ease the worries of merchants and depositors alike.

title: A poor harvest
text: Rain ruins the harvest. Grain prices climb and merchants grow cautious.

title: A busy fair
text: The Frankfurt fair is crowded with buyers, and the house earns good commissions on bills of exchange.

title: Courier robbed on the Mainz road
text: Highwaymen stop the house's courier and take a bag of coin.

title: Unexpected talent
text: One of the children astonishes their tutors. The house may have found its next great banker.

options.label: Send the child to university
options.text: The child is sent to study at Heidelberg, and returns sharper for it.

options.label: Teach them at home
options.text: The child is taught at home by the house's own clerks.

options.label: Let it pass
options.text: The matter is let pass, and the gift fades with the schoolroom.

title: Fever in the house
text: A child of the house falls gravely ill with fever.

options.label: Fetch doctors from Mainz and Heidelberg
options.text: Doctors are fetched from Mainz and Heidelberg at great expense, and the child recovers fully.

options.label: Trust the local physician
options.text: The local physician is trusted with the case.

chance.text: The child lives, but is left sickly.

title: The forgiven clerk
text: The clerk the house forgave has been at the strongbox again, and this time he has fled with what he took.

title: The Senate asks for a gift
text: The Senate of the Free City asks the leading houses for gifts to repair the old bridge over the Main.

options.label: Give 1,500 fl.
options.text: The house's gift is read out in the Senate, and the city remembers it.

options.label: Decline politely
options.text: The house sends its regrets. The Senate notes which houses gave.

title: A pamphleteer comes calling
text: A pamphleteer has heard of the house's recent losses and offers, for a fee, not to print them.

options.label: Pay him 400 fl.
options.text: He is paid, and the pamphlet is never printed.

options.label: Refuse him
options.text: He is shown the door.

chance.text: He prints, and the bourse reads of your losses over its coffee.
chance.miss_text: He goes off to find an easier mark.

title: Gebrüder Winter asks for help
text: The Winter brothers have lent too boldly, and their depositors are at the door. They ask your house, quietly, for 5,000 fl. until the storm passes.

options.label: Lend them 5,000 fl.
options.text: The money goes to the Winters that evening, and they do not forget it.

options.label: Send your regrets
options.text: Your regrets go to the Winters. They will remember that too.

title: Gebrüder Winter repays
text: Gebrüder Winter returns the 5,000 fl. your house lent it, with 250 fl. of interest and its thanks.

title: Albrecht invites you into a syndicate
text: Bankhaus Albrecht is gathering houses to take up a new state loan together, and offers your house a share of 10,000 fl. on the same terms as its own.

options.label: Take a share of 10,000 fl.
options.text: Your house joins the Albrecht syndicate.

options.label: Decline with thanks
options.text: Your house declines. Albrecht finds another partner.

title: The syndicate pays out
text: The state loan is placed with investors, and Bankhaus Albrecht pays out your share: 10,600 fl. for your 10,000.

title: Doubts about Naples
text: Letters from Naples speak of an empty treasury and unpaid troops. Neapolitan bonds are harder to sell.

title: Austrian finances strained
text: Vienna borrows again to cover last year's deficit. Holders of Austrian bonds grow uneasy.

title: Barricades on the Zeil
text: The streets around the counting house are full of armed men, and a barricade goes up at the end of the lane. The Senate has sent to Mainz for troops. What will the house do?

options.label: Hire guards for the counting house
options.text: Armed porters stand at the doors day and night until the troops arrive. Nothing is touched.

options.label: Give the Senate money for the troops
options.text: The house pays toward the soldiers' keep. The Senate remembers it; so do the democrats.

options.label: Bar the doors and wait
options.text: The shutters go up and the clerks are sent home.

chance.text: A crowd breaks into the ground floor, and silver and coin are carried off before the soldiers come.
chance.miss_text: The fighting stays two streets away.
